title: 🔐 Nikhil reused one password... the cost was every other login #passwords #2fa
title_alts: 🔑 Nikhil's leaked password fed credential stuffing... how that works #passwords #privacy
🧯 Nikhil kept one password everywhere... stop the chain reaction #passwords #accounts
description_hook: One password shared across a dozen logins is one leak away from all of them. Here is the order to fix it in.
setting: a home desk with a laptop and a phone
protagonist_type: an ordinary person with too many logins

characters.name: Nikhil
characters.description: thirty-two, short black hair, grey zip hoodie, a chipped enamel mug always within reach

claims.claim: Software tries your pair on hundreds of sites.
claims.basis: round illustrative order of magnitude for automated login attempts, not a measured count

claims.claim: Say you reuse one password across twelve accounts.
claims.basis: round illustrative assumption, stated as such in the narration
arithmetic: all twelve accounts share the single leaked password

claims.claim: Nine doors stay open, all with the same key.
claims.basis: arithmetic: twelve stated accounts minus the three changed in the example

scenes.narration: One leaked password can unlock every account that shares it.
scenes.caption: एक लीक हुआ पासवर्ड हर उस खाते को खोल देता है जहाँ वही लगा है।
scenes.image_brief: A single small brass key lying on a dark wooden desk beside nine identical closed padlocks arranged in a neat row, one warm desk lamp lighting them from the left, deep shadows behind.

scenes.narration: Breached site data gets bundled and sold in bulk lists.
scenes.caption: हैक हुई साइटों का डेटा बड़ी सूचियों में बंडल होकर बिकता है।
scenes.image_brief: A plain text file open on a laptop screen in a dim room, showing a long column of email addresses each followed by a password, the pale screen glow the only light in the room.

scenes.narration: Your email is the username almost everywhere.
scenes.caption: आपका ईमेल लगभग हर जगह यूज़रनेम होता है।
scenes.image_brief: A login form on a phone screen, the phone propped against a kettle on a kitchen counter, the email field already filled in and the password field empty, soft morning light from a window.

scenes.narration: By the end you will know which passwords actually need changing.
scenes.caption: अंत तक आप जान जाएंगे कि कौन-सा पासवर्ड बदलना ज़रूरी है।
scenes.image_brief: Four sticky notes stuck to a fridge door, each with a different website name written on it in marker, two of them crossed out, bright even kitchen light.

scenes.narration: Attackers do not guess. They replay. Software tries your pair on hundreds of sites.
scenes.caption: हमलावर अंदाज़ा नहीं लगाते। सॉफ़्टवेयर सैकड़ों साइटों पर वही जोड़ी आज़माता है।
scenes.image_brief: A laptop screen filled with a fast scrolling list of website names, each line marked with a small red cross, in a dark room lit only by the screen.

scenes.narration: One match logs them in. No alarm sounds, because the password was correct.
scenes.caption: एक जगह मेल खाया और लॉगिन हो गया। कोई अलार्म नहीं बजता।
scenes.image_brief: The same laptop screen and the same list, now stopped, with one line marked by a green tick while every other line keeps its red cross, dark room, screen glow only.

scenes.narration: Say you reuse one password across twelve accounts. One leak exposes twelve.
scenes.caption: मान लीजिए बारह खातों पर एक ही पासवर्ड है। एक लीक से बारहों खुल जाते हैं।
scenes.image_brief: Twelve identical closed padlocks laid out in a grid of four by three on a grey table, one small brass key resting in the middle of the grid, flat even daylight.

scenes.narration: Change it on three. Nine doors stay open, all with the same key.
scenes.caption: तीन बदल दिए? नौ दरवाज़े उसी चाबी से खुले रहते हैं।
scenes.image_brief: The same grey table and grid, but three of the twelve padlocks are now larger and a different shape, the nine matching ones still surrounding the small brass key, flat even daylight.

scenes.narration: Unique passwords do not stop phishing. You can still type one into a fake page.
scenes.caption: अलग पासवर्ड फ़िशिंग नहीं रोकते। नकली पेज पर आप ख़ुद टाइप कर देंगे।
scenes.image_brief: A phone in a desk stand showing a bank login page whose web address in the bar is subtly misspelled, papers and a chipped enamel mug around it, warm evening lamp light.

scenes.narration: And a stolen phone number defeats codes sent by text.
scenes.caption: और नंबर चोरी हो जाए तो एसएमएस के कोड काम नहीं देते।
scenes.image_brief: A phone lying face up on a bedside table showing a text message with a six digit code in it, the rest of the room dark except the screen light on the tabletop.

scenes.narration: Reuse is what turns one company's bad night into your problem.
scenes.caption: दोबारा इस्तेमाल ही किसी कंपनी की गलती को आपकी मुसीबत बनाता है।
scenes.image_brief: A dark server room with two rows of tall machine cabinets, one cabinet door standing open, red and blue status lights reflecting on the polished floor between the rows.

scenes.narration: Unique passwords break that link. A manager remembers them so you do not.
scenes.caption: अलग पासवर्ड यह कड़ी तोड़ देते हैं। मैनेजर उन्हें याद रखता है।
scenes.image_brief: Nine different padlocks of different shapes on a dark wooden desk, each with its own distinct key beside it, and a closed notebook stamped with a lock symbol, warm lamp light.

scenes.narration: Change your email password first. Everything else resets through it.
scenes.caption: पहले ईमेल का पासवर्ड बदलें। बाकी सब उसी से रीसेट होता है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone on a wooden desk showing an email account security screen with a change password button highlighted, a glass of water beside it, soft evening light from a lamp.

title: 📍 Tanvi tapped allow once... the app permission that keeps collecting #privacy #android
title_alts: 🗺 Tanvi's location permission became a daily trail... how that happens #privacy #location
🚫 Tanvi left one permission on always... the setting that fixes it #privacy #apps
description_hook: A permission is not a single yes, it is a standing arrangement. This is how one tap becomes a daily record of where you were.
problem_domain: mobile app permissions and location data
setting: a phone screen and the streets it quietly records
protagonist_type: a phone owner who installs apps without reading

characters.name: Tanvi
characters.description: twenty-six, long hair tied back, olive green jacket, a cracked phone case held together with tape

claims.claim: Your phone can report a location every five minutes.
claims.basis: round illustrative interval chosen for the example, not a platform specification
arithmetic: 1440 minutes in a day divided by the five minute interval already stated

claims.claim: That trail is bundled with thousands of others and sold onward.
claims.basis: illustrative scale for aggregation, deliberately vague because volumes vary by broker

scenes.narration: Permission is not one time. It is a standing invitation.
scenes.caption: परमिशन एक बार की बात नहीं। यह खुला न्योता है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone flat on a wooden table showing a permission dialog with two buttons reading allow and don't allow, a small location arrow icon above them, bright daylight from a window.

scenes.narration: Free apps still have costs. Yours is often the data.
scenes.caption: मुफ़्त एप का भी दाम होता है। वह दाम आपका डेटा है।
scenes.image_brief: An app store listing on a phone screen, the word free in large type under a plain rounded app icon, the phone in a stand on a tidy desk, cool even office light.

scenes.narration: Location, contacts, photos: each one is a separate door.
scenes.caption: लोकेशन, कॉन्टैक्ट, फ़ोटो: हर एक अलग दरवाज़ा है।
scenes.image_brief: Three plain doors side by side in an empty corridor, each with one symbol painted on it, a map pin, an address book and a photograph, even overhead light.

scenes.narration: You will learn which permission to revoke tonight.
scenes.caption: आज रात कौन-सी परमिशन बंद करनी है, यह पता चल जाएगा।
scenes.image_brief: A phone lying on a bedspread showing an app permission list with a column of toggles, one toggle switched off and faintly highlighted, soft lamp light from the side.

scenes.narration: An app with background location can read your position all day.
scenes.caption: बैकग्राउंड लोकेशन वाला एप दिन भर आपकी जगह पढ़ सकता है।
scenes.image_brief: A city map filling a phone screen with a dotted trail of location pins crossing it from one edge to the other, the phone flat on a cafe table beside a saucer, afternoon light.

scenes.narration: That trail is bundled with thousands of others and sold onward.
scenes.caption: वह रास्ता हज़ारों और लोगों के साथ जुड़कर आगे बेचा जाता है।
scenes.image_brief: A large city map mounted on the wall of a windowless room, hundreds of faint dotted trails overlapping across it, lit by a single humming ceiling strip light.

scenes.narration: Your phone can report a location every five minutes.
scenes.caption: फ़ोन हर पाँच मिनट में एक लोकेशन भेज सकता है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone and a small round wall clock side by side on a table, the phone screen showing a list of timestamps five minutes apart each with a location pin, cool daylight.

scenes.narration: That is 288 points a day. Home, work, clinic, all obvious.
scenes.caption: यानी दिन के 288 पॉइंट। घर, दफ़्तर, क्लिनिक, सब साफ़।
scenes.image_brief: A printed sheet pinned to a corkboard covered in 288 small dots, three of them circled in red pen and labelled home, work and clinic, plain desk light from above.

scenes.narration: Maps genuinely need location. Revoking it there breaks the app.
scenes.caption: नक्शे वाले एप को लोकेशन सच में चाहिए। बंद करें तो टूट जाएगा।
scenes.image_brief: A navigation map open on a phone clipped to a car dashboard, a blue route line running up the screen, bright daylight coming through the windscreen onto the dashboard.

scenes.narration: The fix is not deleting everything. It is matching access to purpose.
scenes.caption: सब कुल हटाना हल नहीं। ज़रूरत के मुताबिक़ पहुँच देना हल है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone on a wooden desk showing three location choices listed as never, while using the app, and always, with the middle choice selected, warm light from one side.

scenes.narration: Most apps work fine set to ask every time.
scenes.caption: ज़्यादातर एप हर बार पूँछने वाली सेटिंग पर ठीक चलते हैं।
scenes.image_brief: A phone home screen full of app icons on a white table, a tiny grey location arrow sitting beside every icon except one, soft even daylight from above.

scenes.narration: A one-second tap today decides what leaves your phone for years.
scenes.caption: एक सेकंड का टैप तय करता है कि सालों तक क्या बाहर जाएगा।
scenes.image_brief: A phone resting on a sofa cushion with a permission dialog half faded from the screen, the room otherwise dark except a street lamp glowing through the window.

scenes.narration: Open your location settings. Change any always to while using.
scenes.caption: लोकेशन सेटिंग खोलें। हर हमेशा वाली एप को बदल दें।
scenes.image_brief: A phone held upright in a stand on a bedside table showing a full list of apps with their location settings, several rows reading while using the app, warm lamp light.

title: 📶 Devansh trusted the cafe wifi name... the setting that stops this #publicwifi #privacy
title_alts: 🌐 Devansh's saved wifi list rejoins fakes by name... why that works #publicwifi #wifi
🧹 Devansh never forgot an old hotspot... clear this list tonight #publicwifi #privacy
description_hook: A network name is not proof of anything, and your phone rejoins by name alone. The fix is a list you have never cleaned.
setting: a cafe table, an airport hall and a parked car
protagonist_type: a commuter who connects wherever there is signal

characters.name: Devansh
characters.description: forty, greying temples, navy windbreaker, a laptop bag with one broken zip pull

claims.claim: Say you used airport wifi once, two years ago.
claims.basis: round illustrative timeframe for the example, stated as a supposition in the narration

claims.claim: a saved networks list reduced to three entries
claims.basis: illustrative target number used to make the advice concrete, not a recommendation from any standard

scenes.narration: Anyone can name a hotspot after the cafe next door.
scenes.caption: कोई भी अपने हॉटस्पॉट का नाम पडोस के कैफ़े जैसा रख सकता है।
scenes.image_brief: A chalkboard sign on a cafe counter reading Free WiFi with a network name written under it, a coffee machine and stacked cups behind, warm afternoon light from the front window.

scenes.narration: Your phone keeps a list of networks it trusts.
scenes.caption: आपका फ़ोन उन नेटवर्क की सूची रखता है जिन पर वह भरोसा करता है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone screen showing a long saved networks list with many names stacked down the page, the phone resting on a cafe table beside a half finished coffee, soft daylight.

scenes.narration: It rejoins them by name, silently, whenever one appears.
scenes.caption: नाम देखकर वह चुपचाप दोबारा जुड़ जाता है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone lying face up and untouched on a marble counter with the wifi symbol lit at the top of its screen, bright even light from overhead lamps.

scenes.narration: Which network is the real risk? You will see.
scenes.caption: असली ख़तरा कौन-सा नेटवर्क है? आगे देखिए।
scenes.image_brief: Two identical network names listed one above the other on a phone screen, one with a padlock symbol beside it and one without, the phone on a dark table, cool screen glow.

scenes.narration: A laptop can broadcast that same name from any corner. Your phone matches the name, connects, and routes traffic through it.
scenes.caption: वही नाम कोई लैपटॉप भी चला सकता है। फ़ोन जुड़कर सारा ट्रैफ़िक उसी से भेजता है।
scenes.image_brief: An open laptop on the back seat of a parked car with a small antenna standing beside it, a cafe front visible through the car window, dim interior and bright street outside.

scenes.narration: Say you used airport wifi once, two years ago.
scenes.caption: मान लीजिए दो साल पहले एक बार एयरपोर्ट वाईफ़ाई चलाया था।
scenes.image_brief: An airport departure hall with rows of empty seats and a wall sign showing a wifi symbol above a network name, a suitcase parked by one seat, cold wide ceiling light.

scenes.narration: That name still sits saved. One broadcast and you are back on.
scenes.caption: वह नाम आज भी सेव है। एक बार दिखा और आप जुड़ गए।
scenes.image_brief: A phone tucked in a coat pocket with its screen visible, a connection notice sliding in at the top of the screen, dim evening light on the fabric around it.

scenes.narration: Encrypted sites still protect the contents of what you send. The network still sees where you go.
scenes.caption: कंटेंट तो सुरक्षित रहता है। पर नेटवर्क देखता है कि आप कहाँ गए।
scenes.image_brief: A phone screen split between a padlocked address bar at the top and a plain list of visited site names below it, the phone flat on a wooden desk, one warm lamp at the side.

scenes.narration: Forgetting a network is a privacy setting, not housekeeping.
scenes.caption: नेटवर्क भुलाना सफ़ाई नहीं, प्राइवेसी सेटिंग है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone settings screen with one network selected and a forget this network option highlighted, the phone on a kitchen table beside a set of keys, morning light.

scenes.narration: The shorter your saved list, the fewer names anyone can fake.
scenes.caption: सेव सूची जितनी सीमित, नक़ली नाम बनाने की गुंजाइश उतनी कम।
scenes.image_brief: A phone screen showing a saved networks list with only three entries at the top and empty space below them, the phone on a bedside table under soft lamp light.

scenes.narration: Open saved networks. Delete every one you will not use again.
scenes.caption: सेव नेटवर्क खोलें। जो दोबारा काम नहीं आएंगे, उन्हें हटा दें।
scenes.image_brief: A phone upright in a stand on a desk showing the saved networks list with a delete confirmation box open over it, a notebook beside the stand, warm evening lamp light.

title: 📱 Ishita's codes arrived by text... why that is the weakest 2fa #2fa #onlinesafety
title_alts: 🔁 Ishita's number moved in a sim swap... how the codes follow #simswap #2fa
⛔ Ishita relied on sms codes... the one switch that stops this #2fa #privacy
description_hook: A phone number is issued to you, not owned by you. That single fact is what makes text message codes the weakest second factor.
problem_domain: two factor authentication and number takeover
setting: a mobile shop counter and a bedside table
protagonist_type: a careful saver who did set up two factor

characters.name: Ishita
characters.description: thirty-eight, shoulder length hair with a centre parting, mustard cardigan, reading glasses pushed up on her head

claims.claim: A transfer request needs your name, number, and a few details.
claims.basis: illustrative summary of a verification step, deliberately unspecific because requirements differ by carrier

claims.claim: Two codes later, your email is theirs.
claims.basis: round illustrative count for the example, chosen to show how few steps it takes

scenes.narration: Your phone number is not really yours. It is assigned.
scenes.caption: आपका फ़ोन नंबर असल में आपका नहीं। वह आपको दिया गया है।
scenes.image_brief: A single sim card lying alone on a dark grey desk beside an empty sim tray and a straightened paperclip, one hard overhead light throwing a sharp shadow.

scenes.narration: Every reset link and code you get flows through that number.
scenes.caption: हर रीसेट लिंक और कोड उसी नंबर से होकर आता है।
scenes.image_brief: A phone screen showing a stack of notification cards, each holding a short numeric code, the phone on a bedside table in a dark room lit only by the screen.

scenes.narration: So the number is the master key, quietly.
scenes.caption: यानी वह नंबर चुपचाप मास्टर चाबी बन जाता है।
scenes.image_brief: One large old brass key resting on top of a phone on a wooden table, the phone screen showing a mobile number in a plain input field, warm light from one side.

scenes.narration: You will see how attackers move a number, and what blocks it.
scenes.caption: नंबर कैसे हटाया जाता है और क्या रोकता है, यह देखिए।
scenes.image_brief: A mobile shop counter with a queue rope in front of it, a ticket number display on the wall and a board of sim card offers behind, bright fluorescent ceiling light.

scenes.narration: A transfer request needs your name, number, and a few details.
scenes.caption: ट्रांसफ़र के लिए नाम, नंबर और थोड़ी जानकारी चाहिए होती है।
scenes.image_brief: A printed transfer request form on a shop counter with the name, number and address fields partly filled in, a pen lying across it, hard overhead shop light.

scenes.narration: Approve it wrongly and the codes arrive on their phone instead.
scenes.caption: गलती से मंज़ूरी मिली तो कोड उनके फ़ोन पर जाने लगते हैं।
scenes.image_brief: Two identical phones side by side on a shop counter, only the right one lit with an incoming code message while the left stays dark, cool light from above.

scenes.narration: Say the attacker has your leaked birth date and address.
scenes.caption: मान लीजिए हमलावर के पास आपकी जन्मतिथि और पता है।
scenes.image_brief: A laptop screen showing a table of leaked personal records with name, address and date of birth columns, the room dark apart from the screen glow on the desk edge.

scenes.narration: That is often enough. Two codes later, your email is theirs.
scenes.caption: इतना ही काफ़ी है। दो कोड बाद ईमेल उनका हो जाता है।
scenes.image_brief: A laptop screen showing an email inbox with a password changed notice at the top of the list, in a dark room, the screen light falling on the back of an empty chair.

scenes.narration: Are text codes useless? No. They still beat one factor alone.
scenes.caption: एसएमएस कोड बेकार हैं? नहीं। अकेले पासवर्ड से तो बेहतर हैं।
scenes.image_brief: A phone on a kitchen table showing a two step verification screen with the text message option selected and an app option below it, morning light through a window.

scenes.narration: But an app code lives on the device, not the network.
scenes.caption: पर एप वाला कोड डिवाइस में रहता है, नेटवर्क में नहीं।
scenes.image_brief: A phone flat on an open notebook showing an authenticator app with a six digit code and a small countdown ring beside it, warm desk lamp light from the left.

scenes.narration: The factor you can lose to a phone shop is the weakest one.
scenes.caption: जो फ़ैक्टर किसी दुकान पर खो सकता है, वही सबसे कमज़ोर है।
scenes.image_brief: A closed mobile shop shutter with a sim card poster pasted on it, a street lamp above throwing a cone of light down onto the empty pavement at night.

scenes.narration: An authenticator app cannot be transferred by a stranger's phone call.
scenes.caption: ऑथेंटिकेटर एप किसी अजनबी के फ़ोन कॉल से नहीं बदलता।
scenes.image_brief: A phone in a stand showing an authenticator code, and behind it a landline handset lying off its cradle on the same desk, dim evening light from one lamp.

scenes.narration: Add a port-out PIN with your carrier today.
scenes.caption: अपने ऑपरेटर से पोर्ट-आउट पिन आज ही लगवाएं।
scenes.image_brief: A phone on a desk showing a carrier account security page with a port out PIN field filled with dots, a folded bill envelope beside it, soft daylight from a window.
